title: Local continuity implies bijectivity of products of pinned comparisons
statement: Assume the directed index I, ring diagram R, cocone c, stage i and structure map s₀:X→Spec(R_i) of [def-pc-perfect-hom-continuity-on]. If PerfectHomLocalMap(U,V,m) holds [def-pc-perfect-hom-local-map], and PerfectHomContinuityOn holds on U,V,U∩V, then the underlying function m is bijective.

source.place: Tag 09RE, Mayer--Vietoris induction step; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09RE checked 2026-10-13

proof.text: For a basic map open its local presentation. Use the corresponding continuity hypothesis at its presenting scheme and perfect pair. Every source colimit element has a representative. Move two representatives to a common stage. If their images under m agree, the pinning equations identify the limit Hom images. The eventual-equality clause gives equality at a later stage; injectivity of ident and the cocone equations give equality in d.pt, then injectivity of a gives equality in the source.

For a desired target element use the representative clause starting at i on its image under b. Pull the stage Hom representative back with ident⁻¹ and then with a⁻¹. The pinning equation and injectivity of b give the required preimage. This also handles empty Hom sets.
Induct on the local-map construction. Products preserve injectivity componentwise and preserve surjectivity by choosing the two preimages. Composition with equivalences preserves bijectivity.
